input.quote: 21.2 Each Patty agrees to indemnify each of the other Parties in respect of all costs, expenses, damages and demands, arising out of or in connection with any claim against, or liability of, the latter as an owner of APCN 2 where such claim is made by, or the liability is to, any third party not being a Party hereto and arises out of or in connection with APCN 2 provided that no indemnifying Party shall be obligated to contribute more than its share of liability as per Schedule B.
input.rationale: The only indemnity architecture is consortium-style cost sharing: Subparagraph 21.2 has each Party indemnify the others for third-party claims against them "as an owner of APCN 2", capped at that Party's Schedule B share, and Paragraph 32 is a reimbursement and claims-conduct regime in Schedule B proportions controlled by the Management Committee. Nothing in the Agreement gives us an intellectual-property infringement indemnity from the Party supplying equipment, facilities or software (no infringement or intellectual-property language appears anywhere), and there are no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies or indemnity super-cap. That is the walk-away case of no supplier IP indemnity at all, so the Agreement fails the fallback on a material term. We inserted a single new Subparagraph 21.4 at the fallback level only, rather than reopening the mutual 21.2/Paragraph 32 bargain (which also benefits us) to reach the preferred position.

mappings.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.

proposal.summary: Insert a Subparagraph 21.4 giving Teleglobe an IP infringement indemnity from the supplying Party, with customary exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x annual O&M Costs super-cap.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The existing indemnity architecture (Subparagraph 21.2 and Paragraph 32) only shares third-party ownership claims in Schedule B proportions and gives us no intellectual-property infringement indemnity, so we have added Subparagraph 21.4 at our fallback position: an IP indemnity from the supplying Party with the usual Teleglobe modification, combination and specification exclusions, procure/modify/replace remedies with a refund backstop, and a super-cap of three times our annual O&M Costs.

ops.text: 21.4 Each other Party shall indemnify Teleglobe USA Inc. against any claim by a third party that the APCN 2, or any equipment, facility or software supplied by that Party, infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right, except to the extent the infringement arises from a modification made by Teleglobe USA Inc., from a combination with items not supplied by that Party, or from specifications furnished by Teleglobe USA Inc. The indemnifying Party shall procure the right for Teleglobe USA Inc. to continue using the infringing item, or modify or replace it so that it is non-infringing, and, if none of those remedies is reasonably available, shall refund the amounts paid by Teleglobe USA Inc. in respect of that item. Each indemnifying Party's aggregate liability under this Subparagraph shall not exceed three (3) times the annual O&M Costs payable by Teleglobe USA Inc.
